newsitem.title: USA: Police seek clues in violent deaths of four people.
newsitem.headline: Police seek clues in violent deaths of four people.

text.p: Homicide detectives in the quiet Seattle suburb of Bellevue Monday were investigating the apparently related deaths of four people whose bodies were found in a home and nearby park.

Police declined to identify the victims or say how they were killed but said all four appeared to be homicide victims. A police spokesman said the first body, that of a young woman in her late teens or early 20s, was found near a park trail Sunday by two boys and their mother.
The body was fully clothed but there were "some signs of violence" that led police immediately to conclude the young woman was a homicide victim, said Bellevue Police Lt. Bill Ferguson.
A spokesman for the county coroner said she had been strangled.

Based on identification found on the woman's body, a detective went to a home several blocks away to investigate further. After the doorbell went unanswered, the detective entered the unlocked house and found three more bodies, one male and two female, in two bedrooms upstairs.

Local media reported that the house had been home to a Boeing Co. employee, his wife, who worked for the University of Washington, and their two daughters, one of whom was a high school senior and one a recent graduate.
Ferguson said the crime scenes at the home and in the park were "obviously associated," adding, "the extent of that association we don't know yet."
Bellevue, with a population of 90,000, had only three homicides in all of 1996.
